knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \left(4+x^{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(4+x^{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &= 4\int 1\,\mathrm{d}x+\int x^{3}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &= 4\frac{x^{0+1}}{(0+1)}+\frac{x^{3+1}}{(3+1)}+C \\ &= 4x+\frac{x^{4}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \left(4+t^{6}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t &= \int \left(4+t^{6}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= 4\int 1\,\mathrm{d}t+\int t^{6}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= 4\frac{t^{0+1}}{(0+1)}+\frac{t^{6+1}}{(6+1)}+C \\ &= 4t+\frac{t^{7}}{7}+C\end{aligned}
$$
